summary: Chronicles of the Bomber-Rovers is an educational web prototype that presents the history and scientific contributions of spacecraft through an interactive three-dimensional environment. Users select a mission from an orbital view, follow an animated journey, and examine contextual information about the spacecraft and its discoveries. The catalog covers nine spacecraft or mission entries associated with the Moon, Mars, an asteroid, and interstellar space. The implementation combines browser-based graphics, audiovisual storytelling, and mission information drawn from NASA sources. The team reports a functional prototype with mouse-based exploration, mission animations, information panels, mobile testing on an iPhone, and a virtual reality viewing option. Educational impact and broad device compatibility have not yet been established through formal testing. The next development priorities are to improve visual fidelity, validate usability and accessibility, and assess learning outcomes in representative settings.
details:
Chronicles of the Bomber-Rovers is an interactive educational website that brings the stories of historic spacecraft together in a virtual space museum. It was developed for the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge to help users explore the engineering, discoveries, and legacy of spacecraft associated with missions to the Moon, Mars, an asteroid, and beyond.

How it works. Users begin with a view of the solar system and select a spacecraft. The experience then presents an animated journey and a three-dimensional scene, accompanied by information about the vehicle, its mission, and its scientific contributions. The scenes are illustrative reconstructions rather than precise simulations of spacecraft trajectories or landing procedures.

Benefits and intended impact. The platform brings historical and scientific information into one visual experience designed for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. By connecting a spacecraft’s design with its journey and discoveries, we hope to encourage curiosity about space science and engineering. The project’s educational impact has not yet been measured through a formal study.

Tools and resources. The web application uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the Three.js library for its interface and three-dimensional graphics. We used NASA mission histories and scientific resources to document the spacecraft. Gemini assisted with organizing information; Claude supported programming; and ChatGPT and Codex assisted with writing, research questions, and development. Our team reviewed the resulting content and code.

Creativity and design considerations. Our approach combines mission history with interactive exploration: visitors follow a spacecraft’s journey before encountering it in its destination environment. We considered the scientific and historical significance of each entry, the availability of reliable sources and visual materials, clarity for a general audience, browser access, and the performance demands of 3D content. The prototype includes nine spacecraft or mission entries, from Apollo lunar hardware to the Mars rovers and Voyager 1.
